Got this hidden object game on sale for a very inexpensive price, and it ended up being one of the best HOGs I've played. The character animations are lacking  (in an amusing way) and the story is formulaic, but the background art and actual gameplay have a nice level of polish.

The story follows a doctor who rushes to a mountain hotel after receiving a disturbing call from a patient.
When he arrives, the hotel is mysteriously empty — until the phone in the patient’s room starts ringing.
When he answers, someone tells him: “The game has begun.”
Moments later, a scream echoes through the corridors… and everything begins to unravel.

From that point on, people start dying one by one, with a mysterious figure always one step ahead, taunting us — “Who’s next?”
It gives strong Agatha Christie – And Then There Were None vibes.

For a 2011 game, the visuals are surprisingly beautiful and the atmosphere hooks you right from the beginning.
The puzzles are mentally engaging, and the hidden-object style is quite innovative — I had never seen this approach before.

There’s a map, but although it shows where actions are still needed, it doesn’t let you fast-travel, so expect a bit amount of backtracking.

My only real disappointment was the ending — far too abrupt for the mystery it had been building.

[h2] A Chilling Thriller with A Killer on the Loose! [/h2]
It’s been a while since I last played a hidden object adventure game, so it felt like the right time to play another. This time, I picked one that was okay when I played it a few years ago.

In [i]Mountain Crime: Requital[/i], a doctor named Philip White has been called to come to the White Wolf Hotel to tend to a patient. But, a rock slide collapses the only way in or out of the resort, so you become trapped. Moments after entering the hotel, a man is found bitten by a snake. Throughout your stay, more bodies keep showing up of the guests. A killer is on the loose and must be stopped! How are you involved in this mystery, and can you find the killer in time before you become a victim yourself?

I want to start this review with the positives about this game. Firstly, the graphics are very well done, like many other HOA games. Seeing more 3D character models was a good and interesting choice. Another aspect I liked was that there was voice acting, and it wasn’t that bad. The music and sound design were also really good. Furthermore, I really enjoyed the whodunit-style story; it reminded me of Agatha Christie’s [i]And Then There Were None[/i] or even [i]Clue[/i]. If you want a decent-length experience, this is for you, as the game should take you almost five hours to complete. Overall, the hidden object scenes aren’t too complicated, and neither are the puzzles. However, one puzzle that did take some time to figure out was Katherine’s locket with the different colored jewels.

The only real problem I had with this game was its ending. It does make sense, and it doesn’t just come out of nowhere, but I feel it ends with no satisfying conclusion. Some spoilers, [spoiler]but it turns out the killer is a twin brother of yours you never knew about who killed all the other guests and wants revenge. You got to live an everyday, great life. In contrast, he didn’t, being sick a lot growing up, living in an orphanage, and losing a sister to a horrible fire. He puts you through a game of cat and mouse and frames you in the end, leading to your arrest.[/spoiler] Then, it abruptly ends. I really think a game like this could benefit from a sequel, but as far as I can tell, that won’t happen anytime soon.

This game isn’t bad; it is a good HOA game with an engaging story, intriguing setting and characters, and an excellent mystery. Even with that ending, I would still recommend it.

I am 32 years old.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.

Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.

With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.

After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.

Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.

Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.

Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you.

[code] [b] Mountain Crime: Requital [/b] - детективный квест-приключение от разработчиков Alawar Stargaze, изданное Alawar Entertainment. Игра вышла в Steam в декабре 2011 года и на данный момент имеет чуть более 360 отзывов, по совокупности дающих "очень положительный" рейтинг. Какие неожиданности ожидают нас на этот раз - разбираемся ниже.[/code]

[u] [b] ๑۩۩๑ СЮЖЕТ ๑۩۩๑ [/b] [/u]

Вообще, если охарактеризовать весь сюжет в целом, то можно обойтись одним единственным ёмким словом "карма". Но, так как оно, увы, ничего не расскажет о себе тем, кто в данный квест не играл, хотелось бы остановиться немного подробнее. 

В роли местного врача Вы попадаете в лютую непогоду, и вынуждены остановиться в отеле с необычным названием "Белый волк". Вроде бы, на первый взгляд все выглядит достаточно неплохо - номера обустроены,  даже есть другие постояльцы, но, по неизвестным причинам, толком никакой обслуги. Однако, обстоятельства складываются таким образом, что выбирать особо не приходится, и мы снимаем себе номер на верхнем этаже. 

Приключения, как оно обычно и бывает, не заставляют себя долго ждать. В одном из соседних номеров происходит жуткая трагедия - мужчину кусает взявшаяся неизвестно откуда смертельно-ядовитая змея, и он начинает умирать прямо у нас на глазах. Откуда подобной рептилии взяться в здешних местах? Однако, размышлять некогда, надо спасать человека от верной смерти. Впрочем, барышня из номера напротив, поглядывая из-за приоткрытой двери, явно не горит желанием помочь. Что это - банальная беспомощность, или ей все-таки есть что скрывать? Водоворот событий начинает свой ход. 

[u] [b] ๑۩۩๑ ГЕЙМПЛЕЙ ๑۩۩๑ [/b] [/u]

Mountain Crime: Requital представляет собой классический квест-приключение в жанре point-and-click HOG с элементами детектива в сюжетной канве. Основа геймлпея строится на поиске необходимых по квесту предметов, благодаря которым мы продвигаемся дальше в разгадке сюжетных тайн. Сцены поиска по списку также представлены здесь, правда, выполнены в слегка нетрадиционном стиле - объекты необходимо будет искать не по названию, а по силуэту. В сущности, это не сильно что-то меняет, хотя, если хотите моё мнение, то более классический вариант с названиями мне все-таки больше по душе. Иной раз по очертаниям бывает весьма сложно понять, что именно надо отыскать. Впрочем, головоломкам иного плана (подбор, сопоставление и др.) здесь тоже будет уделено достаточно внимания. 

По ходу истории нам предстоит познакомиться с разными сюжетными персонажами, проводя расследование, отыскивая улики и сопоставляя факты. Имеются небольшие видео-вставки, местами жестковатые, так что детям малого возраста я бы подобный квест все же не рекомендовал. Имеется режим подсказок в случае, если заплутали, а также возможность пропустить особо сложные места. Также в наличии представлена карта местности с интерактивными указателями, где и что необходимо довести до ума. 

Графически игра выполнена весьма симпатично, ни одна локация не вызвала отторжения или нареканий. Звуковое сопровождение здесь тоже довольно простенькое, но вполне дополняющее общую атмосферу мрачной мистики. Разумеется, в наличии также грамотный русский язык.

[h1] Information / Review English [/h1]

Mountain Crime Requital is a Hidden object Crime thriller developed by Alawar Stargaze.

[h1] Gameplay / Story [/h1]

The Weather is bad, but what a good Doctor cannot be deterred from answering a Patient's call. But the Storm cut off your way back to Civilization as Jack. You will quickly find out: Your Patient is already dead, but not by natural circumstances. More deaths follow, but you can only slowly find out what exactly is going on. And worse, you're somehow involved.

A Hidden object puzzle Adventure awaits you, the Story of which is not immediately obvious. You will work it out through numerous Notes that you will find along the Way. And the People you come into contact with, whether alive or dead, provide further Information. In Addition, there are of course many Objects to be found and Puzzles to be solved. At the beginning you decide for yourself whether interesting spots are displayed with glitter by selecting the Mode.

Hidden object scenes do not come with a usual search list. There is a lot lying around in the Scenes, some against the Rules of Gravity, but instead of the search list there is a single Container in which the five or six Objects that you have to find are shown to you by outline. If you put all of them in the Container, it becomes an object that helps you to find your actual inventory Object. Whether you are using the Container to repair a Water tap that then runs and floats something you need or whether you bring a light into a corner, your Actions are always Goal-oriented and you won't find yourself looking for a Screwdriver beforehand with 20 Rubber ducks and clothespins and collect similar rubbish.

The Puzzles are varied and colorfully mixed, both in type and in claim. There is something for everyone, all of them can be skipped and they are well incorporated into the respective game play. The Explanations are sufficient and both beginners and connoisseurs will get their Money's worth here. What is particularly noticeable: Here no Codes are hidden in inexplicable Places: If something has to be opened, then the Solution is usually traceable and not through a Code that was hidden in the Kitchen oven or for which you would otherwise have to perform an illogical Action .

The Hint offers you help in the search Scenes, it shows you outside where there is something to do; shows if necessary which Inventory object can be used where and if there is nothing to do or to find, it will show the Direction that you have to take next. At the same Time there is still the Book. As soon as you have found the map, you will be able to see exactly where you are and where an Action is possible. You have to run yourself, the Map is not clickable, but the Paths are not so endless and although you have to achieve quite a bit of mileage: You don't get the feeling that this is only happening to buy Time.

[h1] Information / Review Deutsch [/h1]

Mountain Crime Requital ist ein Wimmelbild - Krimi, welcher von Alawar Stargaze entwickelt wurde. 

[h1] Gameplay / Story [/h1]

Das Wetter ist schlecht, aber was ein guter Arzt ist, der lässt sich nicht abhalten, dem Ruf eines Patienten zu folgen. Doch durch das Unwetter wird dir als Jack der Weg zurück in die Zivilisation abgeschnitten. Schnell findest du heraus: Dein Patient ist bereits tot, aber nicht durch natürliche Umstände. Weitere Tote folgen, doch was genau abläuft findest du nur langsam heraus. Und schlimmer noch: Irgendwie bist du in die Sache involviert.

Dich erwartet ein Wimmelbild-Puzzle-Abenteuer, dessen Geschichte nicht sofort offensichtlich ist. Du wirst sie dir erarbeiten, durch zahlreiche Notizen, die du auf dem Weg findest. Und auch die Personen, mit denen du es zu tun bekommst, ob lebend oder tot, geben weiteren Aufschluss. Daneben gibt es natürlich viele Gegenstände zu finden und Puzzle zu lösen. Ob interessante Stellen per Glitzern angezeigt werden, entscheidest du selber zu Beginn durch die Modus-Auswahl.

Wimmelbildszenen kommen nicht mit einer üblichen Suchliste einher. Zwar liegt vieles in den Szenen herum, manches auch eher gegen die Regeln der Schwerkraft, aber statt der Suchliste gibt es einen einzelnen Container in dem dir per Umriss die fünf oder sechs Gegenstände angezeigt werden, die du zu finden hast. Legst du alle in den Container wird dieser zu einem Objekt, der dir hilft, dein eigentliches Inventarobjekt zu finden. Ob du nun mit dem Container einen Wasserhahn reparierst, der dann läuft und etwas, was du brauchst, aufschwemmt oder ob du Licht in eine Ecke bringst, immer sind deine Handlungen zielorientiert und auf der Suche nach einem Schraubenzieher wirst du nicht vorher 20 Gummientchen, Wäscheklammern und ähnlichen Müll einsammeln müssen.

Die Puzzle sind vielfältig und bunt gemischt, sowohl in der Art als auch im Anspruch. Es ist für jeden etwas dabei, alle können übersprungen werden und sie sind gut in den jeweiligen Spielverlauf eingearbeitet. Die Erklärungen sind ausreichend und sowohl Anfänger als auch Kenner werden hier auf ihre Kosten kommen. Was besonders auffällt: Hier werden keine Codes an unerklärlichen Stellen versteckt: Wenn etwas geöffnet werden muss, dann ist die Lösung in der Regel nachvollziehbar und nicht durch einen Code, der im Backofen der Küche versteckt wurde oder für den du sonst eine unlogische Handlung vollbringen musst.

Der Hinweis bietet dir Hilfe in den Suchszenen, er zeigt dir ausserhalb an, wo es etwas zu tun gibt; zeigt bei Bedarf welches Inventarobjekt wo genutzt werden kann und wenn es nichts zu tun oder finden gibt, wird er die Richtung anzeigen, die du als nächstes einschlagen muss. Gleichzeitig gibt es noch das Buch. Sobald du die Karte gefunden hast, wirst du dort sehen können, wo genau du bist und wo eine Aktion möglich ist. Laufen musst du selber, die Karte ist nicht anklickbar, aber die Wege sind nicht so endlos lang und obwohl du einiges an Laufleistung zu vollbringen hast: Man bekommt nicht das Gefühl, dass dies nur geschieht, um Zeit zu schinden. 

[h1] Pro [/h1]

+ tolle Krimi-Geschichte
+ schauriger Muiskuntermalung
+ wundervolle Schauplätze
+ viele Rätsel und Wimmelbilder
+ interessante und bizarre Charaktere
+ Sammelkarten

[h1] Kontra [/h1]

- Grafik sieht veraltet aus

[i]Mountain Crime: Requital[/i] is a fun murder mystery that could have been better in some of its execution.

The artwork is wonderfully done and depicts the luxurious atmosphere of the hotel/resort where the majority of the game takes place extremely well. One thing that I absolutely appreciated about the graphics was that this is the first hidden object game I played that had true 1440p support. Most other games do provide the resolution, however, the picture ends up being upscaled with black bars on the side. This game truly filled the screen and kept the picture crisp.

The character artwork also deviates from the standard by using 3D models instead of taking still artwork and animating it. It’s a nice change, although the models aren’t very detailed. They get the work done and are animated pretty well.

The soundtrack is fine for the most part although there were some instances where it would disappear and suddenly come back.

I liked how the hidden object gameplay did something different with the picture wheels instead of providing a list of objects to find. While the main objective was still the same, the presentation was a nice change.

Story-wise… it could have been better. There were some abrupt jumps and reveals that didn’t make sense, and it was fairly easy to determine who the culprit was. However, the ending was a nice change from the usual fare.

An enjoyable game, though I would’ve liked it to have had some of the usual extras such as collectibles or a bonus chapter.
